toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Kepner-Tregoe Problem Analysis and Decision Analysis, using initial evidence only (no catalogue items collected).
output.brief:
The August dip is mainly a cooling failure, not a contractor, kiosk, survey or pricing problem. Chiller CH-2, which serves floors 6-8, failed 4-19 August. Floors 6-8 were 26-29 C in occupied rooms, and 56 of the negative comments mention heat or stuffiness, all from those floors. Floors 6-8 fell to 6.8 for guests checking out 5-20 August and recovered afterwards. Floors 1-5 barely moved (8.6 to 8.5), and their housekeeping, cleanliness, check-in and survey method show no change. Housekeeping pass rates held at 95-96% and cleanliness barely moved, so the Orrin notice is not supported. Kiosk complaints fell, and the survey itself did not change.

Confidence is fairly high on the cooling link, but I did not check the building telemetry or the finance memo. The rate rise may have added to the value-score dip, but it cannot be separated from normal August seasonality.

Next: reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep spare parts on site, and write a cooling-outage guest recovery protocol. Do not serve notice on Orrin, do not pull the kiosks, do not reverse the rate rise yet, and do not exclude August floor 6-8 responses from the GSS. Consider a return-stay offer to affected guests.
